outcome: initial breastfeeding within the golden hour
cohort: The study included 50 pregnant women receiving doula care and 100 pregnant women receiving standard care from the Eastern Province of Saudi Arabia, Al-Ahsa Region.
finding: The study indicated more favorable delivery and postpartum outcomes among women receiving doula care and their infants compared to standard care, primarily by increasing initiated and exclusive breastfeeding rates and reducing postpartum depression.
mod_finding: Regarding mode of delivery, 86% of the doula group had vaginal deliveries compared to 73% of the standard care group, with CS rates of 14% and 27% respectively, though this difference was not statistically significant (P = 0.78).
